html:
Sri Lanka's win in the 1996 Cricket World Cup, beating Australia by seven wickets in the final at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on 17 March 1996.

The tournament was held in Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka, captained by Arjuna Ranatunga, had been seen as an outsider. Its openers, Sanath Jayasuriya and Romesh Kaluwitharana, attacked from the first ball, scoring fast while fielding rules kept most fielders close in the early overs. Other teams had used such tactics before, but this team made them the rule, and one-day cricket changed after it. In the final, Aravinda de Silva scored an unbeaten century.

The win came during the Sri Lankan civil war. Australia and the West Indies refused to play their matches in Colombo after a bombing there, and gave up the points. The title lifted the country's spirits and made cricket a mass passion there, as India's win in 1983 had done in India. It also helped shift the game's money and power toward South Asia.
sum: Sri Lanka's win in the 1996 Cricket World Cup, beating Australia by seven wickets in the final at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore on 17 March 1996.
